senses.gloss:
प्रु प्रु [cf. rt. प्लु], cl. 1. A. प्रवते,
पुप्रुवे, &c., to spring up, jump up; to go,
move: Caus. प्रावयति, -यितुम्, Aor. अपुप्रवत्,
अपिप्रवत्, to reach to, extend as far as (with acc.):
Desid. of Caus. पुप्रावयिषति, पिप्रावयिषति.
प्रू प्रू in कट-प्रू, q. v.

प्रुत्, त्, त्, त्, moving, going, (at the end of comps.;
cf. अन्तरिक्ष-प्˚, उद-प्˚, उपरि-प्˚, कृष्ण-प्˚.)

प्रुथ् प्रुथ्, by some regarded as the
proper form of rt. प्रोथ्, q. v.

प्रुष् 1. प्रुष् [cf. rt. प्लुष्], cl. 5. 9. 10.
P. A. प्रुष्णोति, प्रुष्णुते, प्रुष्णाति,
प्रुष्णीते, प्रुषायति, -ते, प्रोषितुम्, Ved. to
scatter or sprinkle down in drops, rain, shower,
wet, moisten (in these senses probably fr. प्र +
उक्ष्; Sāy. = सिच्); cl. 9. P. प्रुष्णाति, to become
moist or wet, become unctuous; to pour out, sprinkle,
shed, discharge; to fill; cl. 1. P. प्रोषति, to burn (in
this sense probably fr. प्र + 1. उष्); [cf. Old Germ.
frus, ‘to be cold;’ Mod. Germ. frieren, Frost.]

2. प्रुष्, ट्, ट्, ट्, sprinkling, (at the end of comps.;
cf. अभ्र-प्˚, घृत-प्˚.)

प्रुषित, अस्, आ, अम्, sprinkled, wetted, moist-
ened; burning, consuming; (Sāy.) = दग्धुम् प्र-
वृत्तः.
—प्रुषित-प्सु, उस्, उस्, उ, Ved. of a
speckled or dappled aspect, piebald, of a varied hue
(said of the horses of the Aśvins and of Indra; Sāy.
= विचित्र-रूप).
प्रुष्ट, अस्, आ, अम्, burnt, consumed.

प्रुष्टाय, Nom. A. प्रुष्टायते, -यितुम्, to
sprinkle; (probably incorrectly for प्रुष्वाय below.)

प्रुष्व, अस्, m. the rainy season, the rains; the
sun; (आ), f., Ved. a drop of water, a frozen drop
of water, hoar-frost.

प्रुष्वाय, Nom. A. प्रुष्वायते, -यितुम्, to
fall in drops, trickle.
